Subject: Crossbound connectivity recommendation: VPC Peering / PrivateLink / S2S VPN

Sara — thanks for the walkthrough last week. Per our conversation I put together a short evaluation so we can align on a recommended connectivity pattern for your Private deployment of Redwood (VPC + dedicated inference nodes).

Top-level ask: please confirm constraints below so we can lock the design and start a short PoC.

Key constraints we need from you:
- Latency SLO for inference (p50/p95) and acceptable added network latency budget
- Any egress cost restrictions or hard limits for cross-account traffic
- Whether traffic is allowed to traverse your existing MPLS / Direct Connect links
- CIDR ranges we can peer with and whether overlapping CIDRs are a hard blocker
- Compliance needs (PCI / SOC2) that mandate traffic never traverse public internet or that TLS termination must occur in-cust VPC

Initial read: three viable patterns with tradeoffs
1) PrivateLink (AWS Interface Endpoints) — best control surface and minimal routing changes for customers; favorable for restricting inbound access and meeting non-transitive network policies. Regional; good for control plane/API; per-ENI costs and NLB + endpoint hour costs.
2) VPC Peering — lowest latency, simple for same-region high-throughput data-plane; no transitive routing, so does not scale if customer has many VPCs/accounts. Route table updates required.
3) Site-to-site (S2S) VPN — classic option for on-prem connectivity or when customers prefer to keep traffic on their network edge. Lower cost but higher latency and complex for large scale; good as DR/fallback.

Attached: crossbound-arch-decision-matrix.xlsx (decision criteria + rough monthly cost model), redwood_vpc-design-v1.pdf (proposed address plan & NACL/SG examples).

Next steps: once you confirm constraints above we will propose a recommended configuration (one-page decision + Terraform templates) within 3 business days.

Thanks,

Vivek — thanks for the summary and the attachments. Quick answers from our side:

Constraints and requirements:
- Compliance: PCI-DSS scope applies to tokenization path; all traffic carrying PAN/PII must not go over the public internet. TLS in transit is required; we prefer TLS termination in our VPC for audit reasons.
- Latency: target p95 inference latency increase due to network should be <20ms. p50 target is <5ms additional.
- Throughput: expect steady-state 600 rps, peak 2k rps for batch windows.
- Network: we have an existing Direct Connect (dedicated) + AWS Transit Gateway in us-east-1; we also have on-prem lab networks that will initially use S2S VPN.
- CIDRs: we can provide non-overlapping /16 ranges; overlap is a showstopper.
- Timeline: want a pilot in us-east-1 by the start of Q3 (early July).

Notes: we strongly prefer a model that avoids broad route table exposure and minimizes blast radius from a misconfiguration in our VPCs. PrivateLink looked attractive in the demo but we need to confirm throughput and cost. I attached a short internal network diagram for context (att: atlas_net_diagram_v2.png).

Sara Liu
Senior Cloud Network Engineer | Atlas Payments

Vivek / team — I pulled together a technical recommendation based on Sara's constraints. Quoting Sara's key points: 

> "TLS in transit is required; we prefer TLS termination in our VPC for audit reasons."
> "p95 network added latency <20ms; peak 2k rps; prefer to avoid broad route table exposure."

Recommendation (short): Hybrid pattern — PrivateLink for Redwood control/API endpoints + VPC Peering for same-region high-throughput data-plane; S2S VPN used initially for on-prem lab VMs and as a DR/fallback.

Why hybrid?
- PrivateLink (interface endpoints) provides a narrow ingress point (ENI-backed) in the customer's VPC and does not require changing their route tables to allow access to Redwood services. That addresses the "avoid broad route table exposure" ask and reduces blast radius. It also allows you to keep TLS termination in your VPC if we front with a TLS passthrough NLB + target groups that keep TLS to the NLB (we can support mutual-TLS if required).
- VPC Peering is low-latency and has fewer per-request costs than PrivateLink; so when both Redwood and customer VPCs are in us-east-1 and you need sustained high-throughput data (model inputs / large batch payloads), peering is most cost-effective. Caveat: peering is not transitive and requires manual route maintenance; it also requires non-overlapping CIDRs (we have that from Sara).
- S2S VPN: useful for initial lift of on-prem testbeds and for out-of-region labs. It is higher-latency and introduces jitter; thus we should not rely on it for production inference traffic. Use VPN as a secondary path or for admin access.

Operational notes and configs to include in PoC:
- Control plane endpoints (API auth, telemetry) -> PrivateLink (region-specific). Use endpoint service behind NLB with TLS passthrough; advertise ENIs to their VPC.
- Data plane (in-region inference traffic) -> VPC Peering. Configure security groups to allow TLS 443 and TCP 50051 (grpc) as needed.
- Cross-region considerations: for customer VPCs in other regions, replicate PrivateLink endpoints; we should avoid inter-region peering for data plane.
- Fallback path: mesh traffic through Transit Gateway only if customer wants to centralize, but Transit Gateway introduces costs and potential transitive exposure — only recommended if they require many-to-many connectivity.

Approx cost observations (rough monthly):
- PrivateLink: endpoint hours + GB processed on each endpoint; good control but can be 2-4x per-GB cost vs peering for heavy data.
- Peering: minimal hourly cost; more engineering effort to manage routes/ACLs.
- VPN: low baseline cost but consumes more ops time for reliability.

PoC plan (Soojin): 2-week PoC in us-east-1:
- Day 0-2: create PrivateLink endpoint service + NLB + mutual TLS test.
- Day 3-7: create peering connection for data-plane, run 2k rps load tests (measure p50/p95).
- Day 8-10: validate failover to VPN and measure latency/jitter.
- Deliverables: Terraform templates, measured p50/p95 numbers, cost delta spreadsheet.

I'll draft a short runbook for the template changes and security groups.

-Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
